first.rationale: Two of the three current problems are funnel-mechanics problems (activation -6% QoQ, onboarding completion -4% QoQ), and the inherited record points at onboarding friction as the lever with the most direct contact with both. I am verifying the two memories that actually underwrite the action I intend to take (memory_86 on shortening onboarding, memory_31 on signup simplification) rather than the memory attached to the tempting alternative, because verification is only worth spending where it could change what I do. Both are also the stalest and most proxy-laden claims in the set: memory_31 is 64 days old and memory_86 measures completion rate and time-to-value, not qualified revenue. That gap matters. Cutting required fields and steps reliably raises the numbers it is measured on almost by construction, and it can do so by pushing lower-intent accounts through the funnel and by discarding qualification data that sales later needs, which would show up as a completion win and a qualified-revenue loss. I want the original records to tell me whether either experiment tracked anything downstream of activation, and over what window. I deliberately did not pick promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing. memory_73 reports acquisition and revenue lift for price-sensitive SMB, but discount-acquired price-sensitive accounts are the segment least likely to convert into sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and matching an aggressive entrant on price concedes the frame. That is a defensive reflex, not the highest-value use of a non-carrying slot. Standard experiment with a holdout, not a broad rollout: the inherited evidence is suggestive but old and measured on the wrong metric, so I want the design to include a downstream qualified-revenue guardrail and a lead-quality check, not just completion and activation. If verification shows either memory measured only same-week proxies, I will shrink scope and keep the qualification fields that sales depends on. If memory_86 turns out to have tracked revenue and held up, I would widen. memory_91 stays in reserve as the fallback lever if onboarding verification comes back weak, since activation messaging touches the same declining metric without altering the qualification surface.
